name: X with an uppercase Y Construction

dimensions.form: PP headed by with, followed by uppercase + letter name.
dimensions.meaning: Signals uppercase orthography and a proper/institutional sense for the label.
dimensions.function: Disambiguates official or proper-name use from ordinary descriptive use.
dimensions.distribution: Postposed adjunct or parenthetical after a label.

1.specialization: Specifies uppercase orthography for the relevant label using uppercase.

relatedConstructions.notes: Uppercase specification aligns with proper-noun readings.
Uppercase specification often cues proper-name interpretation.

projection.target: When the contrast is literal, uppercase I specifies the same letter shape as capital I. In a spelling instruction this does not tell the listener whether the word is a name. The comparison concerns the literal case instruction.
projection.evidence: The dictionary verifies the written-case contrast. The uppercase substitution is a constructed use.

curious.title: With an uppercase letter
curious.summary: Adding with an uppercase I (or another letter) says a word is written with a capital, which can point to an official or named meaning.
curious.body: Internet with an uppercase I points to the institutional or official sense. Reformation with an uppercase R points to the proper, historical-event sense. When the contrast is literal, uppercase I names the same letter shape as capital I. In a spelling instruction, it doesn't tell the listener whether the word is a name. It only gives the case. The dictionary marks this account as provisional.
curious.try: Say a word and add with an uppercase and its first letter. Does the same instruction work with capital?

teacher.summary: Helps explain with an uppercase letter as a spelling clarification that can point to a proper sense.
teacher.explain: The pattern is a prepositional phrase headed by with, followed by an, uppercase and a letter name. It is postposed after a label or used parenthetically. It specifies uppercase orthography and favours a proper or institutional sense, disambiguating official or proper-name use from ordinary descriptive use. When the contrast is literal, uppercase I specifies the same letter shape as capital I. In a spelling instruction, this does not tell the listener whether the word is a name. This dictionary treats with a capital letter as the variant. This dictionary marks its analysis provisional.
teacher.terms: Uppercase letter is another name for capital letter. This dictionary lists with a capital letter as a variant.
watch_for: A learner might think an uppercase letter must show a name, when in a spelling instruction the phrase only gives the case.
A learner might read the phrase as saying the word is a name, though it can be only a literal case instruction.
teacher.activity: Students write a list of words with the phrase with an uppercase and the initial. They swap capital in for uppercase and check the written form is the same.
